# `Q-3-33` — Unprocessed Insert Markup

> Insert editorial markup `[++ ...]` was not desugared to a
> Span during postprocessing.

## What this means

Quarto supports a small family of editorial-markup constructs
inspired by CriticMarkup: insertions `[++ ...]`, deletions
`[-- ...]`, highlights `[!! ...]`, and comments
`[>> ...]`. The parser emits each as its own AST node type;
postprocessing rewrites those nodes into `Span` nodes with the
right classes (`.quarto-insert`, `.quarto-delete`, etc.) before the writer runs.

This error fires when an `Insert` node survives the
postprocessing pass. The writer does not know how to render the
raw form — only the postprocessed `Span` form.

This is a defensive guard. A document author cannot fix it from
the source.

## Why this happens

Two known triggers:

- **A Lua filter ran after postprocessing** and reintroduced an
  `Insert` AST node.
- **A bug in the postprocessor** that misses some insertions.

## How to fix

If a custom filter is in use, ensure it does not produce
`Insert` AST nodes after postprocessing, or move the filter
earlier in the pipeline so postprocessing runs again.

If no custom filter is in use, report the document at the Quarto
issue tracker.

## Related

- `Q-3-34`, `Q-3-35`, `Q-3-36` — same condition for `Delete`,
  `Highlight`, and `EditComment` markup respectively.
